Cusco · Perú

Cusco’s Plaza de Armas

Portals, churches and a civic square

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Cusco’s main square occupies part of the earlier Inca civic landscape. Its present edges are defined by arcades and two monumental churches. Walk the perimeter before crossing the centre; each corner changes the apparent scale of the cathedral and the neighbouring hills.

Planning your visit

20–40 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Portals, churches and a civic square

Frame the church towers from an arcade corner. Returning to the same spot after crossing the plaza helps identify which façade belongs to the cathedral and which to the Jesuit church.

Getting there

History and local experience

The arcades make a sheltered edge around an exposed centre. Watch where people meet after rain or during a ceremony: the architecture helps explain how the square still works.

Walking route

  1. Plaza de Armas, Centro Histórico del Cusco
  2. Start under the arcades, cross toward the fountain, then return by the cathedral side.
  3. During public ceremonies use the open pavement instead of crossing the procession route.
